title: Choose the cheapest option per year of service

blocks.text: A water utility (invented for this practice) can keep a pumping station running in several ways: rebuild it, overhaul it, or patch it. Each option has a price now, a running cost at the end of each year, and a life in years, after which the utility would do the same thing again. The options last different numbers of years. `present_cost` in the file values one option today.

Write `yearly_cost(price, running, life, rate)`, the level payment at the end of each year of the option's life that has the same present value as the option, and `cheapest(options, rate)`, which returns the name of the option with the lowest yearly cost. `options` maps a name to `(price, running, life)`. The rate can be zero.
Write the yearly cost as a formula first, and check what it becomes at a zero rate. About eight lines.

cases.says: with equal lives, the option with the lower present cost is chosen, at a positive and at a zero rate
a long-lived option with the higher present cost is chosen when its cost per year of service is lower
the yearly cost is the level payment with the same present value, not the present cost divided by the life

origin.section: Equivalent Annual Cost Compares Options With Different Lives

concepts: a level payment for n years is worth the payment times the annuity factor (1 - (1+r)^-n)/r
options with different lives are compared by the level yearly payment with the same present value
